newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips pare losses, Nasdaq almost unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips pare losses, Nasdaq almost unchanged.

text.p: U.S. blue chips pared earlier losses but remained lower as investors shed large-cap companies which have posted strong gains over the past week.

The Dow was off about seven points to 6248. Briefly, it had fallen by almost 20 points but quickly recovered to currently levels. The Nasdaq Composite was a trace higher, up 0.3 to 1263 after shaking off a brief foray into negative territory. Gains from an earlier rally in tech stocks based on strong book-to-bill numbers were almost completely erased.
The long bond was up 11/32 to yield 6.48 percent.

"The Dow is in overbought territory. We don't see much progress until we get some new base-building and for now we don't have any further upside targets," said Harry Laubscher, market strategist for Tucker Anthony.
"But later, the Dow could pare the losses, especially if bonds pick up. But we say, take advantage of strength, because it could be a rough time between now and early December."

Laubscher said he did not think Wall Street was worried about the upcoming release of the PPI and CPI. "There is little expectation of the Fed making a move with the economy still slowing down, so I don't think people are too worried."
